units.zh: 安重誨，其先本北部豪長。
units.en: An Chonghui came from a line of great chiefs among the northern tribes.
units.literal: An Chonghui—his ancestors were originally great chiefs of the northern tribes.

units.zh: 父福遷，為河東將，救兗、鄆而沒。
units.en: His father Fuqian was a Hedong general who perished in the relief of Yan and Yun.
units.literal: His father Fuqian served as a Hedong general and died while rescuing Yan and Yun.

units.zh: 重誨自明宗龍潛時得給事左右。
units.en: Chonghui had served at Mingzong's side since before he took the throne.
units.literal: Chonghui came to attend at the ruler's side from the time when Mingzong was still heir-apparent.

units.zh: 及鎮邢州，以重誨為中門使。
units.en: When Mingzong held Xingzhou, he appointed Chonghui Central Gate commissioner.
units.literal: When he took charge of Xingzhou, Chonghui was made Central Gate commissioner.

units.zh: 隨從征討，凡十餘年，委信無間，勤勞亦至。
units.en: For more than ten years he followed Mingzong on campaign; trust never wavered, and his exertions were beyond measure.
units.literal: Following him on campaigns for more than ten years, trust was never interrupted, and his labor reached the utmost.

units.zh: 洎鄴城之變，佐命之功，獨居其右。
units.en: At the Ye city crisis, his service in securing the throne stood above all others.
units.literal: When the Ye city affair came, his merit in assisting the mandate stood alone at the foremost.

units.zh: 明宗踐祚，領樞密使，俄遷左領軍衛大將軍充職。
units.en: When Mingzong took the throne, Chonghui headed the Privy Council and soon also held the post of senior general of the Left Army Guard.
units.literal: When Mingzong ascended the throne, he headed the Privy Council; soon he was transferred to Left Army Guard senior general while retaining the post.

units.zh: 〈（案：以下有闕文。）〉
units.en: (The text below is lost.)〉
units.literal: (Note: Below there is missing text.)〉

units.zh: 明宗遣回鶻侯三馳傳至其國，侯三至醴泉縣，地素僻，無驛馬，縣令劉知章出獵，不時給馬，侯三遽以聞。
units.en: Mingzong sent the Uighur envoy Hou San post-haste to his homeland. At remote Liquan County there were no relay mounts; the magistrate Liu Zhizhang was out hunting and failed to provide horses promptly, and Hou San reported the delay at once.
units.literal: Mingzong sent the Uighur envoy Hou San on express relay to his country; when Hou reached Liquan County, the place was by nature remote and had no relay horses; magistrate Liu Zhizhang had gone hunting and did not supply horses in time; Hou San immediately reported it.

units.zh: 明宗大怒，械知章至京師，將殺之；
units.en: Mingzong flew into a rage, had Zhizhang shackled and sent to the capital, and meant to put him to death;
units.literal: Mingzong was greatly angered, had Zhizhang shackled and brought to the capital, and was about to execute him;

units.zh: 重誨從容為言，乃得不死。
units.en: Chonghui pleaded for him calmly, and Zhizhang was spared.
units.literal: Chonghui spoke calmly on his behalf, and he thus escaped death.

units.zh: 明宗幸汴州，重誨建議欲因以伐吳，而明宗難之。
units.en: On a visit to Bianzhou, Chonghui urged using the occasion to strike Wu, but Mingzong hesitated.
units.literal: When Mingzong visited Bianzhou, Chonghui proposed taking the opportunity to attack Wu, but Mingzong found it difficult.

units.zh: 其後，戶部尚書李鏻吳諜者言：「徐知誥欲奉吳國以稱藩，願得安公一言以為信。」
units.en: Later Minister of Revenue Li Lin relayed a Wu spy's message: "Xu Zhigao wishes to submit Wu as a tributary state and asks for Lord An's word as assurance."
units.literal: Later, Minister of Revenue Li Lin, through a Wu spy, said: "Xu Zhigao wishes to offer Wu as a vassal state and seeks one word from Lord An as pledge."

units.zh: 鏻即引諜者見重誨。
units.en: Li Lin at once brought the spy before Chonghui.
units.literal: Lin immediately led the spy to see Chonghui.

units.zh: 重誨大喜，以為然，乃以玉帶與諜者，使遺知誥為信，其直千緡。
units.en: Chonghui was delighted, took it for truth, and gave the spy a jade belt to carry to Zhigao as token—worth a thousand strings of cash.
units.literal: Chonghui was greatly pleased, believed it true, and gave the spy a jade belt to send to Zhigao as pledge; it was worth a thousand strings of cash.

units.zh: 重誨為樞密使，四五年間，獨綰大任，臧否自若，環衛、酋長、貴戚、近習，無敢幹政者。
units.en: For four or five years as Privy Council commissioner he held power alone; none among the guards, tribal leaders, imperial kin, or inner circle dared meddle in affairs.
units.literal: As Privy Council commissioner for four or five years, he alone held great power; praise and blame were as he willed; guards, tribal chiefs, noble kin, and close attendants—none dared interfere in government.

units.zh: 弟牧鄭州，子鎮懷、孟，身為中令，任過其才，議者謂必有覆餗之禍。
units.en: His brother governed Zhengzhou, his sons held Huai and Meng, and he was chief councilor himself—responsibilities beyond his gifts; many said ruin was inevitable.
units.literal: His younger brother held Zhengzhou, his sons held Huai and Meng, and he himself was chief councilor; his duties exceeded his talent, and observers said he would surely meet a disastrous fall.

units.zh: 無何，有吏人李虔徽弟揚言於眾云：「聞相者言其貴不可言，今將統軍征淮南。」
units.en: Soon a clerk, younger brother of Li Qianhui, declared in public: "I hear a fortune-teller say his rank is beyond telling—he is about to lead troops against Huainan."
units.literal: Before long a clerk, Li Qianhui's younger brother, proclaimed among the crowd: "I have heard a physiognomist say his nobility is beyond words; he will now command the army to campaign against Huainan."

units.zh: 時有軍將密以是聞，頗駭上聽。
units.en: A military officer secretly reported this, and it greatly troubled the emperor.
units.literal: At the time a military officer secretly reported this to the throne, which greatly alarmed the emperor's ear.

units.zh: 明宗謂重誨曰：「聞卿樹心腹，私市兵仗，欲自討淮南，有之否？」
units.en: Mingzong told Chonghui, "I hear you have gathered partisans and bought weapons on the sly, planning to take Huainan yourself—is that true?"
units.literal: Mingzong said to Chonghui, "I hear you have planted confidants and privately bought arms and armor, intending to campaign against Huainan yourself—is it so?"

units.zh: 重誨惶恐，奏曰：「興師命將，出自宸衷，必是奸人結構，臣願陛下窮詰所言者。」
units.en: Chonghui, in alarm, replied, "Only Your Majesty orders campaigns and commanders; this must be schemers' work—I beg you to trace whoever said it."
units.literal: Chonghui was terrified and memorialized, "Dispatching armies and appointing commanders comes from the imperial mind; this must be villains' fabrication—I beg Your Majesty to interrogate fully whoever spoke thus."

units.zh: 翌日，帝召侍衛指揮使安從進、藥彥稠等，謂之曰：「有人告安重誨私置兵仗，將不利於社稷，其若之何？」
units.en: Next day the emperor called An Congjin, Yao Yanchou, and others and asked, "Someone accuses An Chonghui of hoarding arms to harm the realm—what shall we do?"
units.literal: The next day the emperor summoned Palace Guard commander An Congjin, Yao Yanchou, and others, and said to them, "Someone reports that An Chonghui has privately stored arms and intends harm to the altars of state—what is to be done?"

units.zh: 從進等奏曰：「此是奸人結構，離間陛下勳舊。
units.en: They answered, "This is schemers' slander, meant to part Your Majesty from a loyal veteran.
units.literal: Congjin and the rest memorialized, "This is villains' fabrication, driving a wedge between Your Majesty and your old merit.

units.zh: 且重誨事陛下三十年，從微至著，無不盡心，今日何苦乃圖不軌！
units.en: Chonghui has served you thirty years, rising from nothing, never stinting loyalty—why would he rebel now!
units.literal: Moreover Chonghui has served Your Majesty thirty years, from obscurity to eminence, never failing in devotion—why should he now plot rebellion!

units.zh: 臣等以家屬保明，必無此事。」
units.en: We stake our families on it—there is no such thing."
units.literal: We pledge our households in guarantee—there is surely no such matter."

units.zh: 帝意乃解。
units.en: The emperor's suspicions eased.
units.literal: The emperor's mind was then eased.

units.zh: 重誨三上表乞解機務，詔不允。
units.en: Chonghui three times asked to leave office; the throne refused.
units.literal: Chonghui thrice submitted memorials begging to be relieved of state affairs; the edict did not grant it.

units.zh: 復麵奏：「乞與臣一鎮，以息謗議。」
units.en: He pleaded again in audience: "Grant me a post in one circuit to still the talk."
units.literal: He again addressed the throne in person: "I beg one circuit for your servant to quiet slander."

units.zh: 明宗不悅。
units.en: Mingzong was annoyed.
units.literal: Mingzong was displeased.

units.zh: 重誨奏不已，明宗怒，謂曰：「放卿出，朕自有人！」
units.en: Chonghui kept petitioning until Mingzong snapped, "Go then—I have others!"
units.literal: Chonghui memorialized without cease; Mingzong grew angry and said, "I release you—I have others!"

units.zh: 即令武德使孟漢瓊至中書，與宰臣商量重誨事。
units.en: He sent Martial Virtue commissioner Meng Hanqiong to the Secretariat to discuss Chonghui with the chief ministers.
units.literal: He at once ordered Martial Virtue commissioner Meng Hanqiong to the Secretariat to consult the chief ministers on Chonghui's affair.

units.zh: 馮道言曰：「諸人苟惜安令公，解樞務為便。」
units.en: Feng Dao said, "If you mean to spare Lord An, let him leave the Privy Council."
units.literal: Feng Dao said, "If all wish to spare Lord An, relieving him of the Privy Council would be convenient."

units.zh: 趙鳳曰：「大臣豈可輕動，公失言也。」
units.en: Zhao Feng said, "Great ministers must not be shifted lightly—you misspeak, sir."
units.literal: Zhao Feng said, "A great minister must not be lightly moved—my lord has misspoken."

units.zh: 道等因附漢瓊奏曰：「此斷自宸旨，然重臣不可輕議移改。」
units.en: They told Hanqiong to report, "The decision is yours, Majesty, but do not lightly move a great minister."
units.literal: Dao and the rest therefore added to Hanqiong's memorial, "This decision rests with the imperial mind, yet a great minister must not be lightly discussed for transfer."

units.zh: 由是兼命範延光為樞密使，重誨如故。
units.en: Fan Yanguang was then made co-commissioner; Chonghui kept his post.
units.literal: Thereupon Fan Yanguang was also appointed Privy Council commissioner, and Chonghui remained as before.

units.zh: 時以東川帥董璋恃險難製，乃以武虔裕為綿州刺史，董璋益懷疑忌，遂縶虔裕以叛。
units.en: Eastern Chuan's Dong Zhang held difficult country and defied control; when Wu Qianyu was sent to Mianzhou, Zhang's suspicions deepened and he imprisoned Yu and rebelled.
units.literal: At the time Eastern Chuan commander Dong Zhang relied on rugged terrain and was hard to control; Wuyou Yu was made Mianzhou prefect, and Zhang grew more suspicious, then imprisoned Yu and rebelled.

units.zh: 及石敬瑭領王師伐蜀，峽路艱阻，糧運不繼，明宗憂之，而重誨請行。
units.en: Shi Jingtang's expedition into Shu stalled on bad passes and broken supply lines; Mingzong worried, and Chonghui volunteered to go west.
units.literal: When Shi Jingtang led the imperial army to conquer Shu, the gorge routes were arduous and grain could not follow; Mingzong worried, and Chonghui asked to go in person.

units.zh: 翌日，領數騎而出，日馳數百里，西諸侯聞之，莫不惶駭。
units.en: Next day he rode out with a few escorts, covering hundreds of li a day; western governors were terrified.
units.literal: The next day he led several horsemen and set out, galloping several hundred li a day; western lords hearing of it were all terrified.

units.zh: 所在錢帛糧料，星夜輦運，人乘斃踣於山路者不可勝紀，百姓苦之。
units.en: Cash, grain, and fodder were rushed by night wherever he went; men and horses littered the roads dead beyond count, and the people groaned under it.
units.literal: Wherever he passed, cash, silk, and grain were transported by night; men and horses collapsed dead on mountain roads beyond counting, and the people suffered bitterly.

units.zh: 重誨至鳳翔，節度使朱弘昭延於寢室，令妻子奉食器，敬事尤謹。
units.en: At Fengxiang, commissioner Zhu Hongzhao welcomed him to his private quarters; wife and children served food with deepest respect.
units.literal: When Chonghui reached Fengxiang, military commissioner Zhu Hongzhao received him in the bedchamber and had wife and children present food vessels, serving with utmost deference.

units.zh: 重誨坐中言及：「昨有人讒構，幾不保全，賴聖上保鑒，苟獲全族。」
units.en: Over the meal Chonghui said, "Yesterday slander nearly destroyed me; only the Emperor's grace spared my house."
units.literal: Seated, Chonghui spoke of how "yesterday someone slandered me and I nearly did not survive; relying on the sacred sovereign's protection I barely preserved my clan."

units.zh: 因泣下。
units.en: He wept.
units.literal: He thereupon wept.

units.zh: 重誨既辭，弘昭遣人具奏：「重誨怨望出惡言，不可令至行營，恐奪石敬瑭兵柄。」
units.en: After he left, Hongzhao reported, "Chonghui spoke bitterly in resentment; keep him from the front lest he steal Shi's command."
units.literal: After Chonghui took leave, Hongzhao sent men to memorialize: "Chonghui harbors resentment and spoke evil words; he must not be allowed to reach the camp, lest he seize Shi Jingtang's command."

units.zh: 而宣徽使孟漢瓊自西回，亦奏重誨過惡。
units.en: Xuanhui commissioner Meng Hanqiong, back from the west, also denounced Chonghui.
units.literal: Meanwhile Xuanhui commissioner Meng Hanqiong, returning from the west, also memorialized Chonghui's offenses.

units.zh: 重誨已至三泉，復令歸闕。
units.en: Chonghui had reached Sanquan when orders recalled him to court.
units.literal: Chonghui had already reached Sanquan when he was ordered to return to court.

units.zh: 再過鳳翔，朱弘昭拒而不納，重誨懼，急騎奔程，未至京師，製授河中帥。
units.en: Passing Fengxiang again, Hongzhao shut him out; in fear he raced on, and before the capital an edict made him Hedong commander.
units.literal: Passing Fengxiang again, Zhu Hongzhao refused entry; Chonghui was afraid, spurred his horse on the road, and before reaching the capital was appointed Hedong commander by edict.

units.zh: 既至鎮，心不自安，遂請致仕。
units.en: At his post he could not rest easy and asked to retire.
units.literal: Once at his post he was ill at ease in mind and asked to retire.

units.zh: 製初下，其子崇讚、崇緒走歸河中。
units.en: When the edict issued, sons Chongzan and Chongxu fled to him at Hedong.
units.literal: When the edict first came down, his sons Chongzan and Chongxu fled to Hedong.

units.zh: 二子初至，重誨駭然曰：「渠安得來？」
units.en: At their arrival Chonghui cried, "How did they get here?"
units.literal: When the two sons first arrived, Chonghui said in alarm, "How could they come?"

units.zh: 家人欲問故，重誨曰：「吾知之矣，此非渠意，是他人教來。
units.en: His family asked why; he said, "I know—they did not choose this; someone sent them.
units.literal: The household wished to ask the reason; Chonghui said, "I know already—this is not their wish; others taught them to come.

units.zh: 吾但以一死報國家，餘復何言！」
units.en: I owe the state only my death—nothing more to say!"
units.literal: I will repay the state with death alone—what more is there to say!"

units.zh: 翌日，中使至，見重誨，號泣久之。
units.en: Next day an imperial messenger came and wept long at the sight of him.
units.literal: The next day an imperial messenger came; seeing Chonghui, he wept a long while.

units.zh: 重誨曰：「公但言其故，勿過相湣。」
units.en: Chonghui said, "Speak your errand—do not pity me so."
units.literal: Chonghui said, "Sir, speak only the reason—do not pity me overmuch."

units.zh: 中使曰：「人言令公據城異志矣！」
units.en: The messenger said, "They say you hold the city in rebellion!"
units.literal: The messenger said, "People say my lord holds the city with alien intent!"

units.zh: 重誨曰：「吾一死未塞責，已負君親，安敢輒懷異志，遽勞朝廷興師，增聖上宵旰，則仆之罪更萬萬矣！」
units.en: Chonghui said, "One death cannot answer my debt—I have failed emperor and kin; how dare I rebel and trouble the court and your sleepless nights—my guilt would only multiply!"
units.literal: Chonghui said, "My death alone does not discharge my duty—I have already failed lord and kin; how dare I harbor alien intent, hastily to trouble the court with troops and add to the sacred sovereign's sleepless nights—then my guilt would be ten thousandfold greater!"

units.zh: 時遣翟光鄴使河中，如察重誨有異志，則誅之。
units.en: Zhai Guangye was dispatched to Hedong to probe rebellion and kill him if guilt were found.
units.literal: At the time Zhai Guangye was sent to Hedong, as if to investigate whether Chonghui had alien intent, then execute him.

units.zh: 既至，李從璋自率甲士圍其第，仍拜重誨於其庭，重誨下階迎拜曰：「太傅過禮。」
units.en: Li Congzhang surrounded the house with troops yet bowed in the courtyard; Chonghui descended to return the bow, saying, "Grand Mentor, too much honor."
units.literal: When he arrived, Li Congzhang himself led armored soldiers to surround the residence, yet bowed to Chonghui in the courtyard; Chonghui came down the steps to return the bow and said, "Grand Mentor exceeds propriety."

units.zh: 俯首方拜，從璋以楇擊其首，其妻驚走抱之，曰：「令公死亦不遲，太傅何遽如此！」
units.en: Mid-bow Congzhang smashed his head with a mace; his wife rushed to shield him crying, "Lord An need not die yet—Grand Mentor, why such haste!"
units.literal: As he bowed his head, Congzhang struck it with a mace; his wife ran in alarm to embrace him and said, "My lord's death is not yet late—Grand Mentor, why so hasty!"

units.zh: 並擊重誨妻首碎，並剝其衣服，夫妻裸形踣於廊下，血流盈庭。
units.en: He shattered her skull too, stripped them both, and left husband and wife naked in the hall, blood flooding the court.
units.literal: He struck Chonghui's wife's head as well until it shattered, stripped their clothes, and husband and wife lay naked collapsed in the corridor, blood filling the courtyard.

units.zh: 翌日，副使判官白從璋，願以衣服覆其屍，堅請方許。
units.en: Next day the deputy commissioner and judge Bai Congzhang asked leave to clothe the bodies; only after urgent pleas was it allowed.
units.literal: The next day the deputy commissioner and judge reported to Congzhang, begging to cover the corpses with clothing; only after earnest pleading was it granted.

units.zh: 及從璋疏重誨家財不及數千緡，議者以重誨有經綸社稷之大功，然誌大才短，不能回避權寵，親禮士大夫，求周身輔國之遠圖，而悉自恣胸襟，果貽顛覆。
units.en: His estate proved worth only a few thousand strings; critics said he had saved the dynasty yet aimed too high, clung to power, failed to court the literati or plan for safety, indulged his pride, and was ruined.
units.literal: When Congzhang inventoried Chonghui's household goods they did not reach several thousand strings; observers said Chonghui had great merit in ordering the altars of state, yet his ambition exceeded his talent; he could not avoid clinging to power and favor, failed to personally honor scholar-officials and seek far-reaching plans to preserve himself and assist the state, and instead indulged his own breast entirely, and so met overturn in the end.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：初，知祥將據蜀也，且上表乞般家屬。
units.en: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: When Meng Zhixiang was seizing Shu he asked to move his family.
units.literal: (《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: At first, when Zhixiang was about to hold Shu, he also submitted a memorial begging to move his household.

units.zh: 時樞密使安重誨用事，拒其請，知祥曰：「吾知之矣。」
units.en: Privy Council commissioner An Chonghui ruled and refused; Zhixiang said, "I see."
units.literal: At the time Privy Council commissioner An Chonghui held power and refused the request; Zhixiang said, "I understand already."

units.zh: 因使密以金百兩為賂，重誨喜而為敷奏，詔許之。
units.en: He secretly sent a hundred taels of gold; Chonghui, pleased, memorialized for him and won permission.
units.literal: He therefore secretly sent a bribe of a hundred taels of gold; Chonghui was pleased and memorialized on his behalf; an edict permitted it.

units.zh: 及家屬至，知祥對僚吏笑曰：「天下聞知樞密，將謂天地間未有此，誰知隻銷此百金耶，亦不足畏也。」
units.en: When his kin arrived he laughed to his officers, "The world fears the Privy Council as unmatched—yet a hundred taels of gold buys it off; nothing to dread."
units.literal: When the household arrived, Zhixiang said to his staff with a laugh, "All under heaven hear of the Privy Council and suppose nothing like it exists between heaven and earth—who knew it is dispelled by this hundred taels of gold? It is also not to be feared."

units.zh: 遂守險拒命。
units.en: He then held the mountains and refused obedience.
units.literal: He then held the passes and defied orders.

units.zh: 《五代史闕文》：明宗令翟光鄴、李從璋誅重誨於河中私第，從璋奮楇擊重誨於地，重誨曰：「某死無恨，但恨不與官家誅得潞王，他日必為朝廷之患。」
units.en: (The 《Lost Texts of the History of the Five Dynasties》: Mingzong ordered Zhai Guangye and Li Congzhang to kill Chonghui at his Hedong mansion; Congzhang felled him with a mace; Chonghui said, "I die without regret—only that I did not help the Emperor kill the Prince of Lu; he will plague the court hereafter."
units.literal: (《Lost Texts of the History of the Five Dynasties》: Mingzong ordered Zhai Guangye and Li Congzhang to execute Chonghui at his private residence in Hedong; Congzhang struck Chonghui to the ground with a mace; Chonghui said, "A certain death holds no regret—only I regret not helping the Son of Heaven execute the Prince of Lu; he will surely become the court's calamity in days to come."

units.zh: 言終而絕。
units.en: He died as he spoke.
units.literal: When the words ended he expired.

units.zh: 臣謹案：《明宗實錄》是清泰帝朝修撰，潞王即清泰帝也。
units.en: I note: the 《Veritable Records of Mingzong》 was edited under Emperor Qingtai; the Prince of Lu is Qingtai.
units.literal: Your servant respectfully notes: the 《Veritable Records of Mingzong》 was compiled in the Qingtai emperor's reign; the Prince of Lu is the Qingtai emperor.

units.zh: 史臣避諱，不敢直書。
units.en: The historians evaded taboo and would not name him plainly.
units.literal: The historiographer avoided taboo and dared not write directly.

units.zh: 嗚呼，重誨之志節泯矣！）〉
units.en: Alas, Chonghui's loyal resolve is lost to the record!)〉
units.literal: Alas, Chonghui's integrity of purpose is extinguished!)〉

units.zh: 朱弘昭，太原人也。
units.en: Zhu Hongzhao was from Taiyuan.
units.literal: Zhu Hongzhao was a man of Taiyuan.

units.zh: 祖玟，父叔宗，皆為本府牙將。
units.en: His grandfather Min and father Shuzong were both staff officers of the Taiyuan command.
units.literal: Ancestor Min, father Shuzong—both were junior officers of the native commandery.

units.zh: 弘昭事明宗，在藩方為典客。
units.en: He served Mingzong as guest-reception officer in the prince's domain.
units.literal: Hongzhao served Mingzong; in the frontier post he was guest-reception officer.

units.zh: 天成元年，為文思使，曆東川副使，二年餘，除左衛大將軍，充內客省使。
units.en: Tiancheng 1 he became Literary Thought commissioner; after two years as Eastern Chuan deputy he was Left Guard senior general and Inner Guest Service commissioner.
units.literal: In Tiancheng year 1 he was Literary Thought commissioner; he passed through Eastern Chuan deputy commissioner for more than two years, then was made Left Guard senior general and Inner Guest Service commissioner.

units.zh: 三年，轉宣徽南院使。
units.en: Year 3 he became Southern Xuanhui commissioner.
units.literal: In year 3 he was transferred Southern Xuanhui commissioner.

units.zh: 明宗親祀南郊，弘昭為大內留守，加檢校太傅。
units.en: At Mingzong's southern suburban sacrifice Hongzhao was grand inner custodian and made acting Grand Mentor.
units.literal: When Mingzong personally sacrificed at the southern suburb, Hongzhao was grand inner custodian and was given acting Grand Mentor.

units.zh: 出鎮鳳翔，會朝廷命石敬塘帥師伐蜀，久未成功，安重誨自請西行。
units.en: He took Fengxiang; Shi Jingtang's Shu campaign stalled; An Chonghui volunteered to go west.
units.literal: He went out to hold Fengxiang; the court appointed Shi Jingtang to command troops against Shu; long without success, An Chonghui asked to go west himself.

units.zh: 至鳳翔，弘昭迎謁馬首，請館於府署，妻子羅拜，捧卮為壽。
units.en: At Fengxiang Hongzhao met him on the road, lodged him at his mansion, and had wife and children bow and toast his health.
units.literal: Reaching Fengxiang, Hongzhao met him at his horse's head and asked him to lodge at the commissioner's residence; wife and children kowtowed, raised cups to wish long life.

units.zh: 弘昭密遣人謂敬瑭曰：「安公親來勞軍，觀其舉措孟浪，儻令得至，恐士心迎合，則不戰而自潰也。
units.en: He secretly told Jingtang, "Lord An comes to oversee the army; he acts rashly—if he reaches camp the men may rally to him and you will collapse without fighting.
units.literal: Hongzhao secretly sent word to Jingtang: "Lord An has come in person to comfort the army; observing his conduct he is rash; if he is allowed to arrive, I fear the soldiers' hearts will align with him and the army will collapse without battle.

units.zh: 可速拒之，必不敢前，則師徒萬全也。」
units.en: Turn him back at once—he will not dare advance, and all will be safe."
units.literal: Quickly refuse him—he will surely not advance, and then master and troops will be wholly secure."

units.zh: 敬瑭聞其言大懼，即日燒營遁還。
units.en: Jingtang, terrified, burned camp and retreated the same day.
units.literal: Jingtang, hearing the words, was greatly afraid and that day burned camp and fled back.

units.zh: 重誨聞之，不敢西行，因返旆東還。
units.en: Chonghui, hearing this, dared not go west and turned back east.
units.literal: Chonghui, hearing of it, did not dare go west and therefore turned his banners east.

units.zh: 復過鳳翔，弘昭拒而不納。
units.en: Passing Fengxiang again, Hongzhao shut him out.
units.literal: Passing Fengxiang again, Hongzhao refused entry.

units.zh: 及重誨得罪，其年弘昭入朝，授左武衛上將軍，充宣徽南院使。
units.en: When Chonghui fell, Hongzhao came to court as Left Martial Guard senior general and Southern Xuanhui commissioner.
units.literal: When Chonghui fell from grace, that year Hongzhao entered court and was made Left Martial Guard senior general and Southern Xuanhui commissioner.

units.zh: 長興三年十二月，代康義誠為襄州節度使。
units.en: Changxing 3, month 12, he replaced Kang Yicheng at Xiangyang.
units.literal: In the twelfth month of Changxing year 3 he replaced Kang Yicheng as Xiangzhou military commissioner.

units.zh: 四年，秦王從榮為元帥，屢宣惡言，執政大臣皆懼，謀出避之。
units.en: Year 4 the Prince of Qin Congrong was marshal and spoke threats; ministers feared and sought posts away from court.
units.literal: In year 4 Prince of Qin Congrong was marshal; he repeatedly proclaimed evil words; the chief ministers all feared and plotted to leave and avoid him.

units.zh: 樞密使范延光、趙延壽日夕更見，涕泣求去，明宗怒而不許。
units.en: Commissioners Fan Yanguang and Zhao Yanshou wept daily for release; Mingzong refused in anger.
units.literal: Privy Council commissioners Fan Yanguang and Zhao Yanshou saw the emperor morning and evening in turn, weeping and begging to leave; Mingzong was angry and did not permit it.

units.zh: 延壽使其妻興平公主入言於中，延光亦因孟漢瓊、王淑妃進說，故皆得免。
units.en: Yanshou's wife the Princess of Xingping pleaded within; Yanguang used Meng Hanqiong and Consort Wang—both won leave.
units.literal: Yanshou had his wife Princess of Xingping speak within the palace; Yanguang also advanced persuasion through Meng Hanqiong and Consort Wang—thus both were released.

units.zh: 未幾，趙延壽出鎮汴州，召弘昭於襄陽，代為樞密使，加同平章事。
units.en: Soon Zhao Yanshou went to Bian; Hongzhao was recalled from Xiangyang as Privy Council commissioner with co-chief councilor rank.
units.literal: Before long Zhao Yanshou went out to hold Bianzhou; Hongzhao was summoned from Xiangyang to replace him as Privy Council commissioner and was given co-chief councilor.

units.zh: 十月，范延光出鎮常山，以三司使馮贇與弘昭對掌樞務，與康義誠、孟漢瓊同謀以殺秦王。
units.en: Month 10 Fan Yanguang went to Changshan; Feng Yun shared the Privy Council with Hongzhao; they joined Kang Yicheng and Meng Hanqiong to plot the Prince of Qin's death.
units.literal: In the tenth month Fan Yanguang went out to hold Changshan; Revenue commissioner Feng Yun and Hongzhao jointly held Privy affairs, and with Kang Yicheng and Meng Hanqiong conspired to kill the Prince of Qin.

units.zh: 閔帝即位，弘昭以為由己得立，故於庶事高下在心，及赦後覃恩，弘昭首自平章事超加中書令。
units.en: Emperor Min's accession Hongzhao credited to himself; he dictated policy; after the general amnesty he jumped from co-chief councilor to chief councilor.
units.literal: When Emperor Min ascended, Hongzhao thought he had been enthroned through himself and therefore in common affairs high and low rested in his heart; after the amnesty and broad grace, Hongzhao was first to leap from co-chief councilor to chief councilor.

units.zh: 素猜忌潞王，致其釁隙，以致禍敗。
units.en: He always distrusted the Prince of Lu, widened the breach, and brought disaster.
units.literal: He always suspected the Prince of Lu and provoked their rift, bringing calamity and ruin.

units.zh: 潞王至陝，閔帝懼，欲奔，馳手詔弘昭圖之。
units.en: At the Prince of Lu's arrival in Shan, Emperor Min panicked and meant to flee; he sent an urgent hand edict to Hongzhao to act.
units.literal: When the Prince of Lu reached Shan, Emperor Min was afraid and wished to flee; he sent a hand edict by express to Hongzhao to plot against him.

units.zh: 時將軍穆延輝在弘昭第，曰：「急召，罪我也，其如之何？
units.en: General Mu Yanhui was at his house and said, "They summon in haste—the blame is mine; what now?
units.literal: At the time General Mu Yanhui was at Hongzhao's residence and said, "Urgent summons—the guilt is mine; what is to be done?

units.zh: 吾兒婦，君之女也，可速迎歸，無令受禍。」
units.en: My son's wife is your daughter—fetch her at once lest she be harmed."
units.literal: My son's wife is your daughter—quickly welcome her back, lest she suffer calamity."

units.zh: 中使繼至，弘昭援劍大哭，至後庭欲自裁，家人力止之。
units.en: Messengers followed; Hongzhao drew his sword, wept, and went to the rear court to die; his family restrained him.
units.literal: Imperial messengers came in succession; Hongzhao drew his sword and wept greatly, went to the rear court intending to kill himself, and the household forcibly stopped him.

units.zh: 使促之急，弘昭曰：「窮至此耶！」
units.en: Pressed hard, Hongzhao cried, "Brought to this pass!"
units.literal: The messenger pressed urgently; Hongzhao said, "Reduced to this!"

units.zh: 乃自投於井。
units.en: He threw himself into a well.
units.literal: He thereupon threw himself into a well.

units.zh: 安從進既殺馮贇，斷弘昭首，俱傳於陝州。
units.en: An Congjin killed Feng Yun, took Hongzhao's head, and both were rushed to Shan.
units.literal: An Congjin, having killed Feng Yun, severed Hongzhao's head; both were sent in relay to Shanzhou.

units.zh: 及漢高祖即位，贈尚書令。
units.en: Later Han Gaozu posthumously made him Minister of Works.
units.literal: When Gaozu of Later Han ascended, he was posthumously made Minister of Works.

units.zh: 朱洪實，不知何許人。
units.en: Zhu Hongshi's origins are unknown.
units.literal: Zhu Hongshi—his origin is unknown.

units.zh: 以武勇累曆軍校，長興中，為馬軍都指揮使。
units.en: A career built on valor brought him to Horse Army commander in the Changxing era.
units.literal: By martial valor he rose through military ranks; in Changxing he was Horse Army commander.

units.zh: 秦王為元帥，以洪實驍果，尤寵待之，歲時曲遺，頗厚於諸將。
units.en: As marshal the Prince of Qin favored his daring; seasonal gifts outdid other commanders.
units.literal: When the Prince of Qin was marshal, Hongshi's boldness won special favor; seasonal gifts exceeded those of other generals.

units.zh: 及朱弘昭為樞密使，勢焰尤甚，洪實以宗兄事之，意頗相協。
units.en: Under Privy Council commissioner Hongzhao's peak power, Hongshi treated him as kin and they largely agreed.
units.literal: When Zhu Hongzhao was Privy Council commissioner his power blazed highest; Hongshi treated him as a clan elder and their minds largely aligned.

units.zh: 弘昭將殺秦王，以謀告之，洪實不以為辭。
units.en: Hongzhao told him of the plot to kill the Prince of Qin; Hongshi raised no objection.
units.literal: When Hongzhao was about to kill the Prince of Qin he told Hongshi the plot; Hongshi did not refuse.

units.zh: 時康義誠以其子事於秦府，故恒持兩端。
units.en: Kang Yicheng's son served the Qin mansion, so he straddled both camps.
units.literal: At the time Kang Yicheng had his son serve the Prince of Qin's household, so he always held to both sides.

units.zh: 及秦王兵扣端門，洪實為孟漢瓊所使，率先領騎軍自左掖門出逐秦王，自是義誠陰銜之。
units.en: At the assault on the Duan Gate Meng Hanqiong sent Hongshi's cavalry out the Left Flank Gate against the prince; Yicheng thereafter bore a grudge.
units.literal: When the Prince of Qin's troops knocked at the Duan Gate, Hongshi was sent by Meng Hanqiong and led the cavalry first from the Left Flank Gate to drive off the prince; from this Yicheng secretly resented him.

units.zh: 閔帝嗣位，洪實自恃領軍之功，義誠每言，不為之下。
units.en: Emperor Min's accession made Hongshi proud of commanding the troops; he would not defer to Yicheng.
units.literal: When Emperor Min succeeded, Hongshi relied on his merit in leading the army and would not yield when Yicheng spoke.

units.zh: 應順元年三月辛酉，義誠將出征，閔帝幸左藏庫，親給軍士錢帛。
units.en: Yingshun 1, third month, day xinyou: Yicheng marched; the emperor visited the Left Treasury to pay the troops in person.
units.literal: In the third month of Yingshun year 1, on xinyou, Yicheng was about to campaign; Emperor Min visited the Left Treasury and personally gave soldiers cash and silk.

units.zh: 是時，義誠與洪實同於庫中麵論用兵利害，
units.en: Yicheng and Hongshi argued strategy face to face in the treasury,
units.literal: At that time Yicheng and Hongshi were together in the treasury debating the pros and cons of using troops,

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》云：洪實見軍士無鬥志，而義誠盡將以西，疑其二心。）〉
units.en: (The 《Ouyang History》: Hongshi saw no fighting spirit in the men while Yicheng marched them all west and suspected treachery.)〉
units.literal: (《Ouyang History》 says: Hongshi saw the soldiers lacked fighting spirit, while Yicheng was sending them all west, and suspected divided loyalty.)〉

units.zh: 洪實言：「出軍討逆，累發兵師，今聞小衄，無一人一騎來者。
units.en: Hongshi said, "We have sent army after army against the rebels; now at a small defeat not a rider returns.
units.literal: Hongshi said, "Campaigning against rebels, we have repeatedly sent armies; now we hear a small setback and not one man or horse has come back.

units.zh: 不如以禁軍據門自固，彼安敢徑來，然後徐圖進取，全策也。」
units.en: Hold the palace guards at the gates—they will not dare charge in; then plan our next move—that is the whole strategy."
units.literal: Better to hold the Forbidden Army at the gates and secure ourselves—they would not dare come straight in; then we may slowly plan advance and retreat—the full strategy."

units.zh: 義誠怒曰：「若如此言，洪實反也。」
units.en: Yicheng snapped, "Say that and you are the rebel."
units.literal: Yicheng said in anger, "If such words, Hongshi rebels."

units.zh: 洪實曰：「公自反，誰反！」
units.en: Hongshi shouted, "You are the rebel—not I!"
units.literal: Hongshi said, "You yourself rebel—who rebels!"

units.zh: 其聲漸厲。
units.en: Their voices rose louder.
units.literal: Their voices grew ever sharper.

units.zh: 帝聞，召而訊之，洪實猶理前謀，又曰：「義誠言臣圖反，據發兵計，義誠反必矣。」
units.en: The emperor summoned them; Hongshi pressed his plan and said, "Yicheng accuses me—by his deployments he is the rebel."
units.literal: The emperor heard, summoned and questioned them; Hongshi still argued his former plan and also said, "Yicheng says I plot rebellion; judging by his troop deployments, Yicheng surely rebels."

units.zh: 閔帝不能明辨，遂命誅洪實。
units.en: Emperor Min could not judge; he ordered Hongshi killed.
units.literal: Emperor Min could not clearly distinguish; he thereupon ordered Hongshi executed.

units.zh: 既而義誠果以禁軍迎降潞王，故洪實之死，後人皆以為冤。
units.en: Yicheng soon surrendered the guards to the Prince of Lu; posterity called Hongshi's death a miscarriage of justice.
units.literal: Afterward Yicheng indeed used the Forbidden Army to welcome the Prince of Lu in surrender; therefore Hongshi's death—later men all regarded it as wrongful.

units.zh: 康義誠，字信臣，代北三部落人也。
units.en: Kang Yicheng, style Xinchen, came from the three northern tribal groups.
units.literal: Kang Yicheng, styled Xinchen, was a man of the three tribal groups of northern Dai.

units.zh: 少以騎射事武皇，從莊宗入魏博，補突騎使，累遷本軍都指揮使。
units.en: Young he rode for the Martial Emperor; entering Weibo with Zhuangzong he became a Swift Cavalry officer and rose to command the household guard.
units.literal: In youth he served the Martial Emperor with mounted archery; following Zhuangzong into Weibo he was made Swift Cavalry officer and rose to commander of the native army.

units.zh: 同光末，從明宗討鄴城，軍亂，迫明宗為主，明宗不然。
units.en: At Tongguang's end he followed Mingzong against Ye; mutineers pressed Mingzong to rule and he refused.
units.literal: At the end of Tongguang he followed Mingzong to campaign at Ye city; the army mutinied and forced Mingzong to be ruler; Mingzong did not agree.

units.zh: 義誠進曰：「主上不慮社稷阽危，不思戰士勞苦，荒耽禽色，溺於酒樂。
units.en: Yicheng urged, "The throne ignores peril and the soldiers' pain, drowning in sport and wine.
units.literal: Yicheng advanced and said, "The sovereign above does not consider the altars in peril, does not think of the soldiers' toil, indulges in birds and beasts, and drowns in wine and music.

units.zh: 今從眾則有歸，守節則將死。」
units.en: Follow the crowd and we live; hold to loyalty and we die."
units.literal: Now if we follow the multitude there is return; if we hold to integrity we will die."

units.zh: 明宗納其言，由是委之心膂。
units.en: Mingzong took his counsel and trusted him with his inmost thoughts.
units.literal: Mingzong accepted his words; from this he entrusted him with his innermost counsel.

units.zh: 明宗即位，加檢校司空，領富州刺史，總突騎如故。
units.en: At Mingzong's accession he became acting Minister of Works, governed Fu, and kept the Swift Cavalry.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he was given acting Minister of Works, held Fuzhou, and still commanded the Swift Cavalry.

units.zh: 尋轉捧聖都指揮使，鎮邠州刺史。
units.en: Soon he commanded the Sacred Guard and held Bin.
units.literal: Soon he was transferred to commander of the Sacred Guard and military commissioner of Bin.

units.zh: 明宗幸汴，平朱守殷，改侍衛馬軍都指揮使，領江西節度使。
units.en: At Bian he pacified Zhu Shouyin and became Horse Army commander and Jiangxi commissioner.
units.literal: When Mingzong visited Bian and pacified Zhu Shouyin, he was made Palace Guard Horse Army commander and Jiangxi military commissioner.

units.zh: 車駕歸洛，授侍衛馬步軍都指揮使、河陽節度使。
units.en: Back in Luoyang he held Horse and Foot command and Heyang.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang he was made Palace Guard Horse and Foot commander and Heyang military commissioner.

units.zh: 長興末，加同平章事。
units.en: Late Changxing he became co-chief councilor.
units.literal: At the end of Changxing he was given co-chief councilor.

units.zh: 〈（《玉堂閑話》云：長興中，侍衛使康義誠，嘗軍中差人於大宅充院子，亦曾小有笞責。
units.en: (The 《Idle Talk from the Jade Hall》: Changxing-era commissioner Kang Yicheng once took a man from a great house as yard servant and had him lightly beaten.
units.literal: (《Idle Talk from the Jade Hall》 says: In Changxing, Palace Guard commissioner Kang Yicheng once detailed a man from a great mansion as courtyard servant and had also lightly flogged him.

units.zh: 忽一日，憐其老而詰其姓氏，則曰：「姓康。」
units.en: One day pitying his age he asked his name: "Kang."
units.literal: Suddenly one day, pitying his age, he questioned his surname; he said, "The surname is Kang."

units.zh: 別詰其鄉土、親族、息嗣，方知是父，遂相持而泣，聞者莫不驚異。）〉
units.en: Further questions on home, kin, and children revealed his father; they embraced and wept; all who heard were astonished.)〉
units.literal: Questioning further his native place, kin, and offspring, he then knew it was his father; they thereupon embraced and wept; hearers were all startled.)〉

units.zh: 長興末，加同平章事。
units.en: Late Changxing he became co-chief councilor.
units.literal: At the end of Changxing he was given co-chief councilor.

units.zh: 秦王為天下兵馬元帥，氣焰熏灼，大臣皆懼，求為外任。
units.en: The Prince of Qin became commander of all armies; his arrogance blazed; ministers feared him and sought posts away from court.
units.literal: The Prince of Qin was marshal of all armies under heaven; his arrogance blazed hot; the chief ministers all feared and sought posts away from court.

units.zh: 義誠以明宗委遇，無以解退，乃令其子以弓馬事秦王以自結。
units.en: Favored by Mingzong, Yicheng could not resign; he had his son serve the Prince of Qin in archery and horsemanship to win favor.
units.literal: Yicheng, owing to Mingzong's favor, had no way to resign; he therefore had his son serve the Prince of Qin in archery and horsemanship to curry favor.

units.zh: 明宗不豫，秦王諷義誠為助，義誠曲意承奉，亦非真誠。
units.en: When Mingzong fell ill, the Prince of Qin urged Yicheng to aid him; Yicheng flattered him insincerely.
units.literal: When Mingzong fell ill, the Prince of Qin urged Yicheng to help; Yicheng bent to flatter him, yet it was not sincere.

units.zh: 及朱弘昭、馮贇等懼禍，謀於義誠，但云：「仆為將校，不敢預議，但相公所使耳。」
units.en: When Zhu Hongzhao, Feng Yun, and the rest feared disaster and plotted with Yicheng, he only said, "I am a military officer; I dare not take part in counsel—I do only as the chief councilor orders."
units.literal: When Zhu Hongzhao, Feng Yun, and the rest feared calamity and plotted with Yicheng, he only said, "I am a military officer; I dare not join deliberations—I do only as the chief councilor commands."

units.zh: 及秦王既誅，明宗宴駕，閔帝即位，加檢校太尉、兼侍中，判六軍諸衛事。
units.en: After the Prince of Qin was killed, Mingzong died, and Emperor Min took the throne; Yicheng was made acting Grand Commandant and Palace Attendant and put in charge of the Six Armies and all guards.
units.literal: After the Prince of Qin was executed, Mingzong died, and Emperor Min ascended; Yicheng was given acting Grand Commandant and concurrent Palace Attendant, and directed the Six Armies and all guards.

units.zh: 未幾，鳳翔變起，西軍不利，義誠懼，乃請行，蓋欲盡率駕下諸軍送降於潞王求免也。
units.en: Soon the Fengxiang revolt broke out; the western army fared badly; Yicheng, afraid, asked to march—likely meaning to lead the emperor's troops in surrender to the Prince of Lu to save himself.
units.literal: Before long the Fengxiang revolt rose; the western army fared poorly; Yicheng feared and asked to march—likely intending to lead all troops at the emperor's side in surrender to the Prince of Lu to save himself.

units.zh: 會與朱洪實議事不葉，洪實因厲聲言義誠苞藏之志，閔帝曖昧，不能明辨，而誅洪實。
units.en: He disputed strategy with Zhu Hongshi; Hongshi cried that Yicheng harbored treachery; Emperor Min, confused, could not judge and had Hongshi executed.
units.literal: He happened to dispute strategy with Zhu Hongshi; Hongshi cried out that Yicheng harbored treacherous intent; Emperor Min, bewildered, could not judge clearly and executed Hongshi.

units.zh: 及義誠率軍至新安，諸軍爭先趨陝，解甲迎降，義誠以部下數十人見潞王請罪，潞王雖罪其奸回，未欲行法。
units.en: When Yicheng reached Xin'an, the troops raced to Shan, laid down arms, and surrendered; Yicheng came with several dozen men to beg pardon of the Prince of Lu; though the prince blamed his treachery, he did not yet punish him.
units.literal: When Yicheng led the army to Xin'an, the troops raced ahead to Shan, laid down arms and welcomed surrender; Yicheng came with several dozen followers to beg pardon of the Prince of Lu; though the prince blamed his treachery, he did not yet wish to punish.

units.zh: 清泰元年四月，斬於興教門外，夷其族。
units.en: In the fourth month of Qingtai 1 he was beheaded outside the Xingjiao Gate and his clan was wiped out.
units.literal: In the fourth month of Qingtai year 1 he was beheaded outside the Xingjiao Gate and his clan was exterminated.

units.zh: 藥彥稠，沙陀三部落人。
units.en: Yao Yanchou came from the three Shatuo tribes.
units.literal: Yao Yanchou was a man of the three Shatuo tribal groups.

units.zh: 幼以騎射事明宗，累遷至列校。
units.en: Young he rode for Mingzong and rose to company rank.
units.literal: In youth he served Mingzong with mounted archery and rose through the ranks to company commander.

units.zh: 明宗踐阼，領澄州刺史、河陽馬步都將。
units.en: At Mingzong's accession he held Cheng and commanded Heyang horse and foot.
units.literal: When Mingzong ascended he held Chengzhou and was Heyang Horse and Foot commander.

units.zh: 從王晏球討王都於定州，平之，領壽州節度使、侍衛步軍都虞候。
units.en: With Wang Yanqiu he pacified Wang Du at Ding and received Shou and Foot Army deputy command.
units.literal: Following Wang Yanqiu against Wang Du at Dingzhou, when it was pacified he held Shouzhou and was Palace Guard Foot Army deputy commander.

units.zh: 屬河中指揮使楊彥溫作亂，彥稠改侍衛步軍都指揮使，充河中副招討使，將兵討平之。
units.en: Yang Yanwen's Hedong revolt made him Foot commander and deputy pacifier; he crushed the rebellion.
units.literal: When Hedong commander Yang Yanwen rebelled, Yanchou was made Foot Army commander and Hedong deputy pacification commissioner and led troops to pacify it.

units.zh: 無幾，党項劫回鶻入朝使，詔彥稠屯朔方，就討党項之叛命者，搜索盜賊，盡獲回鶻所貢駝馬、寶玉，擒首領而還。
units.en: Tangut raiders struck the Uighur tribute mission; Yanchou camped at Shuofang, hunted rebels and bandits, recovered the tribute camels, horses, and gems, and returned with chiefs captive.
units.literal: Before long the Tangut raided the Uighur tribute mission to court; an edict ordered Yanchou to camp at Shuofang and pursue the Tangut rebels, search out bandits, recover all the camels, horses, and gems the Uighurs had presented, and return having captured the chiefs.

units.zh: 尋授邠州節度使。
units.en: Soon he was commissioner of Bin.
units.literal: Soon he was made Binzhou military commissioner.

units.zh: 遣會兵製置鹽州，蕃戎逃遁，獲陷蕃士庶千餘人，遣復鄉里。
units.en: Ordered to secure Salt Prefecture, the tribes fled; over a thousand captives were restored to their homes.
units.literal: He was ordered to join forces and establish control at Salt Prefecture; the frontier tribes fled; more than a thousand commoners and soldiers lost to the tribes were recovered and sent home.

units.zh: 受詔與延州節度使，
units.en: He joined the Yanzhou commissioner,
units.literal: He received orders with the Yanzhou military commissioner,

units.zh: 〈（案：原本闕二字。）〉
units.en: (Two characters are missing in the original.)〉
units.literal: (Note: The original text lacks two characters.)〉

units.zh: 進攻夏州，累月不克，兵罷歸鎮。
units.en: to attack Xiazhou; months passed without success; the army withdrew.
units.literal: to attack Xiazhou; for many months they could not take it; the army ceased and returned to post.

units.zh: 閔帝嗣位，與王思同攻鳳翔，為副招討使。
units.en: Under Emperor Min he attacked Fengxiang with Wang Sitong as deputy pacifier.
units.literal: When Emperor Min succeeded, with Wang Sitong he attacked Fengxiang as deputy pacification commissioner.

units.zh: 禁軍之潰，彥稠欲沿流而遁，為軍士所擒而獻之。
units.en: When the palace guard broke, Yanchou tried to flee downstream but soldiers seized and handed him over.
units.literal: When the Forbidden Army collapsed, Yanchou wished to flee downriver but was seized by soldiers and presented.

units.zh: 時末帝已至華州，令拘於獄，誅之。
units.en: The Last Emperor was at Hua; he was jailed and killed.
units.literal: At the time the Last Emperor had reached Hua; he ordered him imprisoned and executed.

units.zh: 漢高祖即位，與王思同並製贈侍中。
units.en: Later Han Gaozu posthumously made him and Wang Sitong Palace Attendants.
units.literal: When Gaozu of Later Han ascended, he and Wang Sitong were both posthumously made Palace Attendant by edict.

units.zh: 宋令詢，不知何許人也。
units.en: Song Lingxun's origins are unknown.
units.literal: Song Lingxun—his origin is unknown.

units.zh: 閔帝在藩時，補為客將，知書樂善，動皆由禮。
units.en: In the prince's domain Lingxun served as guest officer, literate and courteous in all he did.
units.literal: When Emperor Min was still in the frontier post, Lingxun was appointed guest officer; he knew books and loved goodness; every movement followed ritual.

units.zh: 長興中，閔帝連典大藩，遷為都押衙，參輔閫政，甚有時譽，閔帝深委之。
units.en: In Changxing the prince held great commands; Lingxun became chief adjutant, won repute in border affairs, and earned deep trust.
units.literal: In Changxing Emperor Min successively held great frontier posts; Lingxun was promoted chief military adjutant, assisted border government, won timely reputation, and the emperor deeply entrusted him.

units.zh: 及閔帝嗣位，朱、馮用事，不欲閔帝之舊臣在於左右，乃出為磁州刺史。
units.en: At accession Zhu and Feng ruled and ousted old companions; Lingxun was sent to Cizhou.
units.literal: When Emperor Min succeeded, Zhu and Feng held power and did not wish the emperor's old followers at his side; he was sent out as Cizhou prefect.

units.zh: 閔帝蒙塵於衛，令詢日令人奔問。
units.en: In exile at Wei Lingxun sent daily runners to inquire after him.
units.literal: When Emperor Min was driven into hardship at Wei, Lingxun had men run daily to inquire.

units.zh: 及聞帝遇害，大慟半日，自經而卒。
units.en: Hearing of the murder he mourned half a day and hanged himself.
units.literal: When he heard the emperor had been murdered, he grieved greatly half a day and hanged himself.

units.zh: 史臣曰：夫代大匠斫者，猶傷其手，況代天子執賞罰之柄者乎！
units.en: The historian says: Even hewing for a master carpenter cuts the hand—how much more wielding imperial punishments!
units.literal: The historiographer says: One who hews for the master carpenter still injures his hand—how much more one who holds the Son of Heaven's rewards and punishments!

units.zh: 是以古之賢人，當大任、秉大政者，莫不卑以自牧，推之不有，廓自公之道，絕利己之欲，然後能保其身而脫其禍也。
units.en: Ancient worthies in high office humbled themselves, disclaimed ownership, served the public, and shunned private gain—only then did they survive.
units.literal: Therefore the worthies of old, when they held great responsibility and wielded great government, all humbled themselves in self-government, pushed away possession, opened the way of public fairness, and cut off selfish desire—only then could they preserve themselves and escape calamity.

units.zh: 而重誨何人，安所逃死，古語云：「無為權首，反受其咎。」
units.en: What sort of man was Chonghui to escape death? As the proverb says, "Do not lead the power—you will bear the blame."
units.literal: Yet what man was Chonghui, and where could he escape death? The old saying runs: "Do not be the head of power—turn and receive its blame."

units.zh: 重誨之謂歟！
units.en: Does this not fit Chonghui!
units.literal: Is this not Chonghui's case!

units.zh: 自弘昭而下，力不能衛社稷，謀不能安國家，相踵而亡，又誰咎也。
units.en: From Hongzhao on, none could guard the realm or steady the state—they fell one after another; who else was to blame?
units.literal: From Hongzhao downward, their strength could not defend the altars, their plans could not settle the state—they perished in succession; upon whom else lay the blame?

units.zh: 唯令詢感故君之舊恩，由大慟而自絕，以茲隕命，足以垂名。
units.en: Only Lingxun, honoring old grace, died by his own hand in grief—a name that endures.
units.literal: Only Lingxun, moved by his old lord's former grace, through great grief cut off his own life; by this death his name may be handed down.

units.zh: 晉王遣都將李嗣昭、李存審、王建及率師來援同州，戰於城下。
units.en: The Prince of Jin sent Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji to relieve Tongzhou and battle was joined under the walls.
units.literal: The Prince of Jin sent commanders Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji with troops to relieve Tongzhou; they fought below the walls.

units.zh: 夏四月己巳，晉王即唐帝位於魏州，改天祐二十年為同光元年。
units.en: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Prince of Jin took the Tang throne at Weizhou, renaming Tianyou 20 Tongguang 1.
units.literal: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Prince of Jin assumed the Tang throne at Weizhou, changing Tianyou 20 to Tongguang 1.

units.zh: 時晉王方攻鎮州，故思遠乘虛以襲之，陷成安，而思遠遂急攻德勝北城，晉將李存審極力拒守。
units.en: While the Prince of Jin besieged Zhenzhou, Siyuan took Cheng'an and stormed Desheng’s north wall; Li Cunshen held firm.
units.literal: At the time the Prince of Jin was attacking Zhenzhou; hence Siyuan seized the opening to strike, took Cheng'an, and then urgently attacked Desheng’s northern city; Jin commander Li Cunshen resisted with utmost strength.

units.zh: 二月，晉王以兵至，思遠收軍而退，復保楊村。
units.en: In the second month the Prince of Jin came up; Siyuan withdrew to Yang village.
units.literal: In the second month the Prince of Jin arrived with troops; Siyuan gathered the army and withdrew, again holding Yang village.

units.zh: 唐帝棄德勝之北城，並軍保楊劉。
units.en: The Tang emperor abandoned Desheng’s north wall and concentrated at Yangliu.
units.literal: The Tang Emperor abandoned Desheng’s northern city and combined the army to hold Yangliu.

units.zh: 六月乙亥，唐帝引軍援楊劉，潛軍至博州，築壘於河東岸。
units.en: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang emperor relieved Yangliu while secretly fortifying east of Bozhou.
units.literal: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang Emperor led troops to relieve Yangliu, secretly moving the army to Bozhou and building ramparts on the river’s east bank.

units.zh: 秋七月丁未，唐帝引軍沿河而南。
units.en: On dingwei in the seventh month the Tang emperor led his army south along the river.
units.literal: On dingwei in the seventh month of autumn the Tang Emperor led troops south along the river.

units.zh: 庚寅，唐帝軍於胡城，先鋒將康延孝率百騎奔於唐，盡泄其軍機。
units.en: On gengyin at Hucheng vanguard Kang Yanxiao defected with a hundred riders and betrayed Liang dispositions.
units.literal: On gengyin the Tang Emperor’s army was at Hucheng; vanguard commander Kang Yanxiao led a hundred horsemen to defect to Tang and fully revealed our military plans.

units.zh: 甲戌，唐帝引師襲中都，王彥章兵潰，於是彥章與監軍張漢傑及趙廷隱、劉嗣彬、李知節、唐文通、王山興等皆為唐人所獲。
units.en: On jiaxu the Tang emperor stormed Zhongdu; Yanzhang’s army broke; he, Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, and others were taken.
units.literal: On jiaxu the Tang Emperor led troops to strike Zhongdu; Wang Yanzhang’s army collapsed; thereupon Yanzhang, army supervisor Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, Liu Sibin, Li Zhijie, Tang Wentong, Wang Shanxing, and others were all captured by Tang men.

units.zh: 帝置傳國寶於臥內，俄失其所在，已為左右所竊迎唐帝矣。
units.en: He laid the seal in his chamber; it vanished—courtiers had stolen it to greet the Tang emperor.
units.literal: The Emperor placed the dynastic seal in the sleeping chamber; soon it lost its place—it had already been stolen by attendants to welcome the Tang Emperor.

units.zh: 唐帝入宮，妃郭氏號泣迎拜。
units.en: The Tang emperor entered the palace; Consort Guo wept and bowed in welcome.
units.literal: The Tang Emperor entered the palace; consort Guo wailed and came forward to bow.

units.zh: 唐帝初入東京，聞帝殂，憮然歎曰：「敵惠敵怨，不在後嗣。
units.en: Entering the Eastern Capital, the Tang emperor learned of the Last Emperor’s death and sighed: "Grudges need not pass to sons.
units.literal: When the Tang Emperor first entered the Eastern Capital and heard the Emperor had died, he sighed in dejection: "Enemy kindness and enemy hatred do not lie in later generations.

units.zh: 九月庚寅，以供奉官郎公遠充契丹歡好使。
units.en: On gengyin in the ninth month Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was sent as envoy of goodwill to the Khitan.
units.literal: On gengyin in the ninth month, Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was made Khitan Goodwill envoy.

units.zh: 龍德二年春正月，戴思遠率師襲魏州。
units.en: In the first month of Longde 2 Dai Siyuan raided Weizhou.
units.literal: In the first month of spring of Longde 2, Dai Siyuan led troops to raid Weizhou.

units.zh: 尋詔河南尹張全義收葬之，其首藏於太社。
units.en: He ordered Zhang Quanyi to bury the body; the head was kept at the Grand Altar.
units.literal: Soon an edict ordered Henan Intendant Zhang Quanyi to collect and bury him; his head was stored at the Grand Altar.

units.zh: 先是，繼韜父嗣昭為潞州節度使，戰歿於鎮州城下，晉王欲以嗣昭長子繼儔襲父位。
units.en: His father Li Sizhao had held Luzhou and died at Zhenzhou; the Prince of Jin meant to give the post to eldest son Jichou.
units.literal: Earlier, Jiyao’s father Sizhao was Luzhou military commissioner and fell in battle below Zhenzhou city; the Prince of Jin wished to let Sizhao’s eldest son Jichou succeed his father’s post.

units.zh: 朕與梁主十年對壘，恨不生見其面。」
units.en: We fought ten years; I regret never meeting him alive."
units.literal: I and the Liang ruler faced each other in battle ten years, regretting I did not see his face in life."

units.zh: 以天雄軍節度使石敬瑭為御營使。
units.en: Shi Jingtang of Tianxiong became imperial camp commissioner.
units.literal: Tianxiong army military commissioner Shi Jingtang was made imperial camp commissioner.

units.zh: 乙酉，前蔡州刺史董璋權知宣義軍軍州事。
units.en: On yiyou, Dong Zhang, former prefect of Cai, was given acting charge of Xuanyi Army affairs.
units.literal: On yiyou, former Cai prefect Dong Zhang was made acting Xuanyi Army military and prefectural commissioner.

units.zh: 二月甲申，晉王攻我黎陽，劉鄩拒之而退。
units.en: On jiashen in the second month, the Prince of Jin attacked Liyang; Liu Xun held him off and forced a withdrawal.
units.literal: On jiashen in the second month, the Prince of Jin attacked our Liyang; Liu Xun resisted him and drove him back.

units.zh: 貞明三年春正月戊午，以前淄州刺史高允奇為右羽林統軍。
units.en: On wuwu in the first month of Zhenming 3, Gao Yunqi, former Inspector of Zi Prefecture, was appointed commander of the Right Feathered Forest.
units.literal: On wuwu, in the first month of spring of Zhenming 3, former Zi Prefecture Inspector Gao Yunqi was made commander of the Right Feathered Forest.

units.zh: 壬戌，幽州節度使趙德鈞兼北面行營招討使，鎮州節度使範延光加檢校太傅。
units.en: On renxu Zhao Dejun of Youzhou became northern campaign commissioner and Fan Yanguang of Zhen inspector grand mentor.
units.literal: On renxu, Youzhou military commissioner Zhao Dejun was given added northern campaign headquarters commissioner; Zhen prefecture military commissioner Fan Yanguang was given Inspector Grand Mentor by inspection.

units.zh: 壬午，以前蔚州刺史張溫為振武留後，以左右廂突陣指揮使康義誠為汾州刺史，以左右廂馬軍都指揮使索自通為忻州刺史。
units.en: On renwu, Zhang Wen, former prefect of Weizhou, was made acting military commissioner of Zhenwu; Kang Yicheng, commander of the left and right wing assault formations, was made prefect of Fenzhou; and Suo Zitong, cavalry commander-in-chief of the left and right wings, was made prefect of Xinzhou.
units.literal: On renwu, former Weizhou prefect Zhang Wen was made Zhenwu acting military commissioner; left-and-right wing assault-array commander Kang Yicheng was made Fenzhou prefect; left-and-right wing cavalry commander Suo Zitong was made Xinzhou prefect.

units.zh: 以河東掌書記馮道為戶部侍郎，充翰林學士；
units.en: Hedong secretary Feng Dao became vice minister of revenue and Hanlin academician;
units.literal: Hedong secretarial aide Feng Dao was made vice minister of revenue and Hanlin academician;

units.zh: 同光元年春正月丙子，五台山僧獻銅鼎三，言於山中石崖間得之。
units.en: In spring of Tongguang 1, on bingzi in the first month, monks of Mount Wutai presented three bronze tripods, saying they had found them in the stone cliffs of the mountains.
units.literal: In spring of the first year of Tongguang, on the first month, day bingzi, monks of Mount Wutai presented three bronze tripods, saying they had obtained them from among the stone cliffs in the mountains.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：潞王至靈寶，思立謀固守陝城以俟康義誠。
units.en: (From the Comprehensive Mirror: When Prince Lu reached Lingbao, Sili planned to hold Shaan city and await Kang Yicheng.
units.literal: (From the Comprehensive Mirror: When the Prince of Lu reached Lingbao, Sili planned to hold Shaan city firm and await Kang Yicheng.

units.zh: 先是，捧聖五百騎戍陝，為潞王前鋒，至城下，呼城上人曰：「禁軍十萬已奉新帝，爾輩數人奚為！
units.en: Earlier, five hundred Pingsheng cavalry had garrisoned Shaan as the Prince of Lu's vanguard. Reaching the foot of the wall, they shouted up, "A hundred thousand men of the imperial guard have already acclaimed the new emperor. What are you few men still doing here!
units.literal: Earlier, five hundred Pingsheng horsemen garrisoned Shaan as the Prince of Lu's vanguard; reaching below the wall, they called to those above: "The imperial army of a hundred thousand has already honored the new emperor—what are you few men doing!

units.zh: 乙亥，翰林學士、戶部侍郎、知制誥馮道，翰林學士、中書舍人趙鳳，俱以本官充端明殿學士。
units.en: On yihai Feng Dao and Zhao Feng, Hanlin academicians, became Duanming Hall academicians at rank.
units.literal: On yihai, Hanlin academician, Revenue vice minister, and edict drafter Feng Dao and Hanlin academician and Secretariat drafting officer Zhao Feng were both made Duanming Hall academicians at their present ranks.

units.zh: 二月乙巳，王晏球奏，此月三日收復定州，獲王都首級，生擒契丹托諾等二千餘人。
units.en: On yisi in the second month Wang Yanqiu reported recovering Ding on the third, taking Wang Du's head and capturing over two thousand Khitan including Tuonuo alive.
units.literal: Second month, yisi: Wang Yanqiu memorialized that on the third of this month Ding prefecture had been recovered, Wang Du's head was taken, and more than two thousand Khitan including Tuonuo were captured alive.

units.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：尚書兵部宣露布於樓前，宣訖，尚書刑部侍郎張文寶奏曰：「逆賊王都首級請付所司。」
units.en: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》 says War at the Secretariat proclaimed the bulletin at the tower; when it ended Zhang Wenbao of Punishments asked that Wang Du's head be given to the proper office."
units.literal: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》: The Ministry of War of the Secretariat proclaimed the victory bulletin before the tower; when the proclamation ended, Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments Zhang Wenbao memorialized: "The rebel Wang Du's head is requested to be delivered to the relevant office."

units.zh: 辛酉，帝御咸安樓受定州俘馘，百官就列，宣露布於樓前，禮畢，以王都首級獻於太社。
units.en: On xinyou Mingzong at the Xian'an Tower received Ding captives, proclaimed the victory bulletin, and offered Wang Du's head at the Grand Shrine.
units.literal: On xinyou, the Emperor took the Xian'an Tower to receive Ding captives and heads; the hundred officials took their places; the victory bulletin was proclaimed before the tower; when the rite was finished, Wang Du's head was offered at the Grand Shrine of State.

units.zh: 王都男四人、弟一人，禿餒父子二人，並磔於市。
units.en: Wang Du's four sons and brother and the Tu Nei father and son were dismembered in the market.
units.literal: Wang Du's four sons, one younger brother, and the father-and-son pair Tu Nei were all dismembered in the market.

units.zh: 大理卿蕭希甫受之以出，獻於郊社，其王都男並蕃將等磔於開封橋。）〉
units.en: Judicial review director Xiao Xifu took it out and offered it at the suburban altars; Wang Du's sons and Tangut generals were dismembered at Kaifeng Bridge.)〉
units.literal: Director of the Court of Judicial Review Xiao Xifu received it and went out, offered it at the suburban altars, and Wang Du's sons and the Tangut generals were dismembered at Kaifeng Bridge.)〉

units.zh: 丙申，詔鄴都、幽、鎮、滄、邢、易、定等州管內百姓，除正稅外，放免諸色差配，以討王都之役，有挽運之勞也。
units.en: On bingshen Mingzong remitted extra levies in Yedu, You, Zhen, Cang, Xing, Yi, and Ding beyond regular tax after the Wang Du campaign's transport burden.
units.literal: On bingshen, an edict for the commoners within the circuits of Yedu, You, Zhen, Cang, Xing, Yi, and Ding, besides regular tax, remitted every sort of differential levy, because of the labor of hauling in the campaign against Wang Du.

units.zh: 以皇子河南尹、判六軍諸衛事從厚為北京留守；
units.en: Prince Conghou of Henan became Beijing regent;
units.literal: the prince, Henan intendant judging the Six Armies and all guards Conghou, was made Beijing regent;

units.zh: 庚子，皇第二子金紫光祿大夫、檢校司徒從榮可檢校太保、同平章事、天雄軍節度使、鄴都留守。
units.en: On gengzi the second prince Li Congrong—Gold and Purple Glory grand master and acting Minister of Education—could become acting Grand Guardian, co-equal councilor, Tianxiong commissioner, and Yedu regent.
units.literal: On gengzi, the Emperor's second son, Gold and Purple Glory Grand Master, acting Minister of Education Li Congrong could be made acting Grand Guardian, co-equal Chief Councilor, Tianxiong military commissioner, and Yedu regent.

units.zh: 丙子，以北京副留守、太原尹孟知祥為檢校太傅、同平章事、成都尹、劍南西川節度副大使、知節度事、西山八國雲南都招撫等使；
units.en: On bingzi Meng Zhixiang—northern deputy regent and Taiyuan prefect—became acting Grand Tutor, chancellor, Chengdu prefect, Jiannan Xichuan vice commissioner and acting commissioner, and pacification commissioner for the western mountains and Yunnan;
units.literal: On bingzi, northern capital deputy regent and Taiyuan prefect Meng Zhixiang was made acting Grand Tutor, co-equal chief minister, Chengdu prefect, Jiannan Xichuan military vice commissioner, acting commissioner, and commissioner for pacification of the western mountains' eight states and Yunnan and the rest;

units.zh: 中和末，以太原李克用兵勢方盛，與定州王處存密相締結。
units.en: Late in the Zhonghe era, fearing the rising power of Li Keyong of Taiyuan, Keju secretly allied himself with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.
units.literal: Late in Zhonghe, because Li Keyong of Taiyuan's military power was then flourishing, he secretly formed a pact with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.

units.zh: 克用怒，加兵討之。
units.en: Keyong was furious and sent additional troops to punish him.
units.literal: Keyong was enraged and added troops to campaign against him.

units.zh: 赫連鐸據雲中，屢引匡威與河東爭雲、代，並兵積年。
units.en: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into conflict with Hedong over Yunzhou and Daizhou; their armies fought for years.
units.literal: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into contest with Hedong over Yun and Dai; their armies clashed for years.

units.zh: 可舉慮其窺伺山東，終為己患，遂遣使構雲中赫連鐸乘其背，則與鎮州合謀舉兵，兼言易、定是燕、趙之餘，雲得其地則正其疆理而分之。
units.en: Keju feared that Keyong would turn his ambitions toward the eastern provinces and become a lasting threat. He sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to attack Keyong from the rear, then conspired with the forces of Zhenzhou to raise troops. He argued that Yizhou and Dingzhou were the last holdings of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yunzhong gained those lands their boundaries could be redrawn and the territory divided.
units.literal: Keju feared that Keyong would watch for an opening in the Shandong region and in the end become a threat to him; he therefore sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to strike from the rear, then conspired with Zhenzhou to raise troops, also saying that Yi and Ding were the remnant territories of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yun gained those lands their boundaries could be rectified and divided.

units.zh: 景福初，鎮州王鎔誘河東將李存孝。
units.en: Early in the Jingfu era Wang Rong of Zhenzhou won over the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Jingfu reign, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou enticed the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.

units.zh: 二年春，河東復出師井陘，再乞師，匡威來援。
units.en: In the spring of the second year Hedong again marched through Jingxing Pass. Wang Rong again appealed for help, and Kuangwei came to his aid.
units.literal: In spring of the second year Hedong again marched out through Jingxing; Rong again begged for troops, and Kuangwei came to his aid.

units.zh: 己卯，以武德使孟漢瓊為右衛大將軍、知內侍省，充宣徽北院使。
units.en: On jimao Meng Hanqiong became right guard senior general, acting palace attendant director, and northern palace bureau commissioner.
units.literal: On jimao Martial Virtue commissioner Meng Hanqiong was made Right Guard senior general, acting Director of Palace Attendants, Northern Palace Bureau commissioner.

units.zh: 辛巳，以捧聖嚴衛左廂馬步軍都指揮使李從璋領饒州刺史，充大內皇城使。
units.en: On xinsi Li Congzhang, Left Wing commander of the Support-the-Sacred Guard, became Rao prefect and inner-palace commissioner.
units.literal: On xinsi, Support-the-Sacred Strict Guard Left Wing horse-and-foot commander Li Congzhang was made Rao prefect and charged as inner-palace commissioner.

units.zh: 以汝州防禦使趙延壽為河陽節度使，以比部郎中、知制誥劉讚為中書舍人，以河陽掌書記程遜為比部員外郎、知制誥，以代州刺史李德充為蔚州刺史。
units.en: Zhao Yanshou, Ru defense commissioner, became Heyang commissioner; Liu Zan, Bureau of Revenue director and edict drafter, became Secretariat drafting officer; Cheng Xun, Heyang secretary, became Bureau of Revenue vice director and edict drafter; Li Dechong of Dai became Yu prefect.
units.literal: Ruzhou defense commissioner Zhao Yanshou was made Heyang military commissioner; Bureau of Revenue director and edict drafter Liu Zan was made Secretariat drafting officer; Heyang secretary Cheng Xun was made Bureau of Revenue vice director and edict drafter; Dai prefect Li Dechong was made Yu prefect.

units.zh: 時李嗣源總帳下親軍攻東北隅；
units.en: Li Siyuan led the household guard against the northeast corner;
units.literal: Li Siyuan commanded the personal troops below the tent attacking the northeast corner;

units.zh: 李嗣源壞夾城東北隅，率先掩擊，梁軍大恐，南向而奔，投戈委甲，噎塞行路，斬萬餘級，獲其將副招討使符道昭洎大將三百人，芻粟百萬。
units.en: Li Siyuan breached Jiacity's northeast and charged in; Liang panicked and fled south, shedding arms until the road jammed; over ten thousand were killed; Fu Daozhao and three hundred officers were taken, with a million bundles of fodder.
units.literal: Li Siyuan broke the northeast corner of Jiacity and led the assault; the Liang army was greatly terrified and fled south, casting weapons and armor; the road was choked; more than ten thousand were beheaded; deputy pacification commissioner Fu Daozhao and three hundred great generals were captured, and a million measures of fodder.

units.zh: 五月辛未朔，晨霧晦暝，帝率親軍伏三垂崗下。
units.en: At the xinwei new moon in the fifth month, thick morning fog hid Cunxu's personal troops below Sanchui Ridge.
units.literal: On the first day xinwei of the fifth month, morning fog dark and dim, the Emperor led his personal army in ambush below Sanchui Ridge.

units.zh: 時嗣源遙領鎮州，詰旦，議欲歸藩，上章請罪，安重誨以為不可，語在《明宗紀》中。
units.en: Siyuan still held Zhen at a distance; at dawn he debated returning to his post and asked punishment; An Chonghui forbade it—the account is in the 《Mingzong Annals》.
units.literal: At the time Siyuan held Zhenzhou at a distance; at dawn he debated returning to his circuit and submitted a memorial asking punishment; An Chonghui held it impossible—the account is in the 《Mingzong Annals》.

units.zh: 秦王從榮素驕，自為河南尹，典六軍，拜大元帥，唐諸大臣皆懼禍及，思自脫，獨義誠心結之，遣其子事秦王府。
units.en: Prince of Qin Congrong was proud. As Henan governor he held the Six Armies and the title Grand Marshal. Tang’s ministers feared ruin and tried to slip away—only Yicheng tied himself to Congrong and sent his son into the prince’s household.
units.literal: The Prince of Qin Congrong had always been arrogant. As Henan governor he controlled the Six Armies and was made Grand Marshal; the great ministers of Tang all feared disaster and sought to escape—only Yicheng bound his heart to Congrong and sent his son to serve in the Prince of Qin’s household.

units.zh: 丙辰，以秘書監呂琦為禮部侍郎，歸德軍節度使趙在禮改天平軍節度使，昭義軍節度使兼侍衛親軍馬步軍都虞候杜重威改忠武軍節度使，忠武軍節度使、侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使劉知遠改歸德軍節度使，前河陽節度使兼奉國左右廂都指揮使侯益改昭義軍節度使。
units.en: On bingchen Lü Qi, palace library director, became vice minister of rites; Zhao Zaili of Guide became Tianping military commissioner; Du Chongwei of Zhaoyi became Zhongwu military commissioner; Liu Zhiyuan of Zhongwu became Guide military commissioner; and Hou Yi, former Heyang commissioner, became Zhaoyi military commissioner.
units.literal: On bingchen, Lü Qi, Director of the Palace Library, was appointed Vice Minister of Rites; Zhao Zaili, Military Commissioner of the Guide Army, was changed to Military Commissioner of the Tianping Army; Du Chongwei, Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi and Chief Adjutant of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot, was changed to Military Commissioner of the Zhongwu Army; Liu Zhiyuan, Military Commissioner of the Zhongwu Army and Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot, was changed to Military Commissioner of the Guide Army; Hou Yi, former Military Commissioner of Heyang and Commander of the Left and Right Wings of the Fengguo Army, was changed to Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi.

units.zh: 李式、翟光鄴為樞密使，王景崇為宣徽使，餘官各有署置。
units.en: Li Shi and Zhai Guangye were made commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Wang Jingchong palace commissioner, and the remaining posts were each filled.
units.literal: Li Shi and Zhai Guangye were made commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Wang Jingchong was made palace commissioner, and the remaining offices were each filled.

units.zh: 會契丹主死，其汴州節度使蕭翰謀歸北地，慮中原無主，軍民大亂，則己亦不得按轡徐歸矣；
units.en: When the Khitan ruler died, his Bianzhou military commissioner Xiao Han planned to return north. He feared that with no ruler in the Central Plains and army and people in chaos, he himself could not withdraw at leisure;
units.literal: When the Khitan ruler died, his Bianzhou military commissioner Xiao Han planned to return north and feared that with no ruler in central China and army and people in great disorder, he himself would be unable to rein in his horse and withdraw at leisure;

units.zh: 光業以書呈樞密承旨李虔徽。
units.en: Guangye presented the letter to Secretariat drafter Li Qianhui.
units.literal: Guangye presented the letter to Secretariat drafter Li Qianhui.

units.zh: 會朝廷再發中使荀鹹乂將兵赴閬州，光業謂虔徽曰：「鹹乂未至，吾父必反。
units.en: When the court again sent the inner envoy Gou Xianyi with troops to Langzhou, Guangye told Qianhui: "Before Xianyi arrives my father will rebel.
units.literal: When the court again sent inner envoy Gou Xianyi with troops to Lang Prefecture, Guangye told Qianhui: "Before Xianyi arrives my father will rebel.

units.zh: 以北京副留守馮贇為宣徽使、判三司。
units.en: Beijing deputy regent Feng Yun became palace treasury commissioner and revenue overseer.
units.literal: Beijing deputy regent Feng Yun was made Palace Treasury Commissioner and overseer of the Revenue Commission.

units.zh: 孟漢瓊被甲乘馬，召馬軍都指揮使朱洪實，使將五百騎討從榮，從榮方據胡床，坐橋上，遣左右召康義誠。
units.en: Meng Hanqiong donned armor, mounted his horse, and summoned Horse Army Commander Zhu Hongshi to lead five hundred cavalry against Congrong. Congrong was lounging on a camp chair on the bridge and sent attendants to summon Kang Yicheng.
units.literal: Meng Hanqiong donned armor and mounted a horse, summoned Horse Army Commander Zhu Hongshi, and ordered him to lead five hundred cavalry against Congrong. Congrong was just then reclining on a folding chair, seated on the bridge, and sent his attendants to summon Kang Yicheng.

units.zh: 端門已閉，叩左掖門，從門隙窺之，見朱洪實引騎兵北來，走白從榮，從榮大驚，命取鐵掩心擐之，坐調弓矢。
units.en: The main gate was shut; he knocked at the Left Flank Gate and peered through the crack, saw Zhu Hongshi leading cavalry northward, and ran to warn Congrong. Congrong was terrified, ordered iron breastplates brought and put on, and sat stringing his bow.
units.literal: The Gate of Correct Deportment was already closed; he knocked at the Left Flank Gate and peered through the crack, saw Zhu Hongshi leading cavalry northward, ran to report to Congrong. Congrong was greatly alarmed, ordered iron breastplates brought and donned, and sat adjusting bow and arrows.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒·明宗紀》云：己丑，大漸，秦王從榮入問疾，帝俯首不能舉。
units.en: (The Comprehensive Mirror, annals of Mingzong, records that on jichou the emperor's illness grew grave. Prince Qin Congrong came to inquire after him, but the emperor could only bow his head and could not lift it.
units.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror·Annals of Mingzong states: On jichou the illness grew grave. Prince Qin Congrong entered to inquire after the emperor's health; the emperor bowed his head and could not raise it.
